titre: The design system becomes a file the agent reads, and that gets checked
essentiel: Google (DESIGN.md), NN/g (UX.md) and Figma (Specs) converge: the design deliverable becomes a file AI can read.
Agent drift is now measured: Rico claims Claude Code follows a design system 31.6% of the time, Mantis flags colors within ΔE 5 of a token.
Design work is moving into the product itself: a canvas plugin for Claude Code, GitHub's Replica, Framer driven over MCP from a phone.

syntheses.titre: The design system is written to be read by a machine
syntheses.texte: Souharda Mukherjee notes that Google, NN/g and Figma landed in the same place within six months: a file AI reads, not a deck. Workshopr shows what that looks like in practice: tokens named by their job and a comment that forbids the agent from "restoring" a color that breaks AA contrast. GitHub goes the same way with Replica, which prototypes from the team's own components and documentation. As a counterpoint, Hani Husamuddin reminds us that the human handoff (three-layer variables, 1:1 Tailwind v4 mapping) is still the foundation the agent reuses.

Two tools publish numbers on the gap between what the agent generates and the system. Rico claims Claude Code follows a provided design system only 31.6% of the time (vendor figure, to be checked) and offers a check before shipping. Mantis learns a live app's style and flags "almost right" values (#465569 instead of #475569, 15px instead of 16px). Workshopr adds a third route: write the contrast ratio into the token's comment so nobody has to trust their eyes.

syntheses.titre: Design happens in the product, not only in the mockup
syntheses.texte: Raya B. built a Claude Code plugin that turns any page into a canvas: you edit real components with their props, with accessibility checks running continuously. Ayoub Kada describes a flow with no handoff: key screens in Figma, sent to Claude through the MCP, "the real build, never a prototype". Iliyass Oulad edits a Framer site from his phone via the official MCP, but keeps art direction at his desk. All of them keep a human review step.

posts.role: Lead Product Designer, AI-ready design systems (Dubai)
posts.idee: The new design deliverable isn't a deck, it's a file AI reads. Google open-sourced DESIGN.md, NN/g proposes UX.md, Figma launched Specs: three teams, same conclusion in six months.
concret: DESIGN.md (Google): how the product should look
UX.md (Nielsen Norman Group): research, vocabulary and user context for AI
Figma Specs: design language documented for people and agents
Test: screenshots of the design system instead of the file produce approximated colors, gaps and text styles
posts.commentaires: Open question: where does your design reasoning live, and can a machine read it?
posts.engagement: Posted less than an hour ago

posts.role: Newsletter by a designer turned design engineer
posts.idee: The token file is the proof of the move to design engineering. The author publishes his platform-tokens.css: five reds named by their job and comments addressed to whoever, person or agent, opens the file next.
concret: --brand, --brand-ink (5.02:1), --brand-line, --brand-soft, --brand-tint
"Do not restore" comment: the old shade breaks AA contrast on every primary button
Contrast ratio written in the comment, pointer to a dated audit
973-line file, nothing redacted

posts.idee: GitHub open-sources Replica, an AI prototyping tool fed by the team's design system. You describe an interface in the Copilot app and a running prototype appears alongside, built with existing components, patterns and docs.
concret: MIT license, github/replica repository
Canvas plugin for the Copilot app, starter apps, self-hosted Replica Hub for comments
Local: Copilot app, Git and Node.js on macOS or Linux
Limit: not production-ready; accessibility and interactions must be assessed separately

posts.idee: A design system handoff is prepared for humans before agents. He shares a full Figma file, a made-up bus booking app, to show how he hands a system to a Tailwind CSS v4 team.
concret: 75 variables in 3 layers: primitives, semantic (light/dark), component
Seat component with Status × Type variants and a Focus property
No state relies on color alone (check, dashed edge, hatching)
Tokens mapped 1:1 to Tailwind CSS v4, keyboard-navigable demo, free on Figma Community

posts.idee: AI doesn't design, it averages. Rico pitches itself as design infrastructure for coding agents: it gives the agent taste rules, then checks every screen before shipping.
concret: Claimed figure: Claude Code follows a provided design system 31.6% of the time (vendor measurement)
Claimed blind test: 9 out of 10 people pick Rico
742 users claimed, free: tryrico.com

posts.role: Full-stack engineer, creator of Mantis (open source)
posts.idee: Your agent wrote #465569, your token is #475569. Nobody will see it, your design system will. Mantis learns an app's real style and flags almost-right values.
concret: mantis learn: walks every route, screen size and theme, records colors (with CSS variables), sizes, radii, spacing, motion
"Off-style" warning when a color is within ΔE 5 of a house color without being one
Test on 5 sites: 0 warnings on tailwindcss.com and vercel.com, 2 on stripe.com, 4 on linear.app and github.com
posts.commentaires: Reshared by MergeWatch: review moves from "does it render?" to "does it keep the product's constraints?".

posts.idee: The visual layer Claude Code was missing. Her plugin turns any browser page into a canvas: edit by hand or with Claude, on real components, and the change lands in the code.
concret: Edit real components with their real props
Edits constrained by the design system, Figma file import
Accessibility checks while designing
Change delivered in the right files, ready for review

posts.idee: I don't hand off anymore. His flow: key screens in Figma, sent to Claude via the Figma MCP, ask for the real build and never a prototype, motion with Higgsfield, iterate on every detail, ship.
concret: Figma MCP + Claude for the build
Higgsfield for motion
Article "Designers don't hand off anymore (part 1)"

posts.idee: A client update done on a café terrace, from a phone. Claude, connected to Framer through the official MCP, changes the headline and adds a section in three messages; he reviews and approves.
concret: Official Framer MCP usable from the browser or the phone
On Mac: going from Figma to Framer through the MCP
Stated limit: art direction still happens at the desk
